name: @viberaven/mcp

tools.name: viberaven_check_readiness
tools.description: Useful before an AI-built app on Vercel and Supabase launches or is handed off. Runs the local `viberaven check` (no login, no API key, no telemetry), which reads the repository for launch gaps (missing RLS in migrations, leaked secrets, unbounded queries, unsigned webhooks) and writes a prioritized task list to .viberaven/agent-tasklist.md plus a verdict to .viberaven/gate-result.json. This is advice, not a gate: the user decides when to ship. It reads repo files and does not query the live database.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to the MCP server cwd.

tools.name: viberaven_rls_test
tools.description: After reviewing a Supabase migration or ownership policy, optionally execute already reviewed local permissions scenarios for owner, other_user and anon. Returns Pass, Fail or Unknown per cell with the original scoped evidence. This is an experimental PGlite imitation, not live Supabase proof. The optional PGlite dependency must already be installed next to the matching CLI used by this local MCP host; missing setup returns the CLI setup guidance as a tool error. No SQL, credentials, provider calls or dependency installation are accepted.

matrix.description: Path to an already reviewed permissions JSON file, relative to cwd or absolute. Expectations must describe intended access.

migrations.description: Local migrations directory. Defaults to supabase/migrations under cwd.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to the MCP server working directory.

tools.name: viberaven_verify
tools.description: Re-run the local VibeRaven check after you apply fixes. Call this once per batch of fixes (not after every edit) to update .viberaven/gate-result.json and confirm whether the gate moved toward clear.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to the MCP server cwd.

tools.name: viberaven_audit
tools.description: Run local Vercel + Supabase production checks: table RLS presence, policy quality, view/function boundaries, service-role boundaries, and Vercel pooler usage. Call this when the project uses Supabase or Vercel and you need a focused infra audit beyond the general readiness check. Pass json: true for machine-readable output.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to current working directory.

tools.name: viberaven_init_rules
tools.description: Install bounded VibeRaven agent-instruction rules into native AI instruction files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / .cursor/rules), so coding agents know when a VibeRaven pass applies. Use dryRun: true to preview first.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to current working directory.

tools.name: viberaven_clean_plan
tools.description: Write a non-destructive cleanup plan for generated .viberaven artifacts and logs. Call this when the .viberaven directory has grown stale. Does not delete anything; it only produces a reviewable plan.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to current working directory.

tools.name: viberaven_strict_gate
tools.description: Run `viberaven --strict --json` and return the verdict from .viberaven/gate-result.json (gate.status is clear, warning or not_clear). Useful before a deploy or CI run when the user wants the verdict as JSON. The user decides whether to ship.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to the MCP server cwd.

tools.name: viberaven_gate_result
tools.description: Run a fresh local scan (`viberaven --json`) and return the verdict it writes to .viberaven/gate-result.json (gate.status is clear, warning or not_clear). It rewrites the .viberaven artifacts; it does not read an older result without scanning.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to the MCP server cwd.

tools.name: viberaven_context_map
tools.description: Refresh and return .viberaven/context-map.json, a compact summary of the last scan for the next agent step. Use this to load minimal context before acting on a gap.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to the MCP server cwd.

tools.name: viberaven_actions
tools.description: Read the current chat-native action surface from .viberaven/actions.json. Use this to list stable, referenceable action IDs the user can verify or refer to by name.

cwd.description: Project root. Defaults to current working directory.

tools.name: viberaven_verify_action
tools.description: Verify or explain the lifecycle state of a stable VibeRaven action ID (format VR-A<number>). Use this when the user references a specific action and you need its current state.

tools.name: viberaven_heal_plan
tools.description: Write a non-destructive heal plan (.viberaven/heal-plan.md) for a specific gap or target file, to review before viberaven_heal_apply. The plan names the target and the verify command. For rls_disabled it also shows the new migration it would write and its SQL, or why it will not write one; other gaps get no patch preview. Does not modify source files.

target.description: Target file path for the heal.

tools.name: viberaven_heal_prompt
tools.description: Return an agent-ready prompt that fixes a specific gap. Use this when you want a coding agent to apply the fix itself rather than using the guarded recipe.

target.description: Target file path for the heal.

tools.name: viberaven_heal_apply
tools.description: Apply a guarded repo-code heal recipe for a supported gap. Only call this after viberaven_heal_plan. Pass yes: true to skip confirmation. The rls_disabled recipe writes a migration that enables row level security with no policies, so browser reads of those tables return no rows until policies exist: call it only after the user agrees. Its task leaves out yes: true; pass yes: true only once the user agrees. Returns the applied change summary, with any warnings.

target.description: Target file path for the heal.

tools.name: viberaven_validate_npm_package
tools.description: Look up npm package names on the public registry (registry.npmjs.org). Returns not_found when the registry has no such package or cannot be reached, suspicious when the registry answers with an error other than 404, and suspicious when the package was first published less than 14 days ago and its name is within 2 character edits of a popular package (a typosquat signal), or when it has an empty description, no listed maintainers and 3 or fewer published versions. Anything else is ok, which only means none of these signals fired; it is not a security review of the package. Useful when an agent is about to add a dependency the project has not used before.

packageName.description: Single npm package name to validate.

packageNames.description: Multiple package names to validate in one call.

tools.name: viberaven_work_start
tools.description: Save a versioned Task contract and run a free local check without login, network, edits or payment. Prefer contract; request alone saves a draft with unknown acceptance. No credentials or shell command fields. Review the returned contract before approving resume. Resume shares its short request and redacted results with the account; the full definition stays local. Provider and non-local contracts are planning only.

contract.title: VibeRaven Task contract v1
contract.description: Declarative task definition, not executable commands or evidence. Runtime also enforces a 4800-byte UTF-8 limit and condition IDs unique across both lists.

tools.name: viberaven_work_resume
tools.description: Resume the SAME saved task through account sign-in, quota or payment. Set approvedContract=true only after explicit human approval of its exact acceptance, must-not-break conditions and declared scope. A draft can be upgraded with contract before any job exists; its request must stay identical. Never authorize sign-in or payment for the person. Execution state is separate from independent verification observations; agent success is not condition proof. Scope declarations are not an enforced sandbox.

contract.title: VibeRaven Task contract v1
contract.description: Declarative task definition, not executable commands or evidence. Runtime also enforces a 4800-byte UTF-8 limit and condition IDs unique across both lists.

tools.name: viberaven_work_status
tools.description: Read the saved Task contract, execution state and independent verification receipts locally without account, network, edits or payment. Current worktree changes invalidate checked proof; missing observations stay not_checked. Checked conditions separately report passed/failed outcomes. Historical agent results do not verify conditions.

tools.name: viberaven_work_prepare
tools.description: Before implementing a local Node feature, freeze reviewed expected behavior and actual dirty/untracked baseline. Supports module comparisons, sequential HTTP requests to an isolated local server factory, and frozen Node preservation tests. No login or network; no commands or imported proof. MCP plans are limited to 4800 UTF-8 bytes; larger plans use the CLI JSON file (65536 bytes). No browser, database or live provider proof. Changed plans require a new task.

verification.title: VibeRaven local verification plan v1
verification.description: Reviewed local observations, not commands or imported proof. Runtime also bounds JSON depth/UTF-8 bytes, including HTTP request/expected bodies to 8192 bytes, rejects unknown condition IDs, and restricts node-test to preservation conditions and frozen test-owned paths. HTTP factories return unlistened Node servers; sequential requests observe volatile state only. Runtime package/config files remain candidate inputs. Expected values remain in the host comparator. Coverage completeness is a human judgment.

tools.name: viberaven_work_verify
tools.description: Run or resume the SAME frozen plan using the locally available pinned Docker image only. Set approvedVerification=true only after human review/approval. Network is disabled and no dependencies are installed. No login or billing. Missing conditions, dependencies or Docker remain not_checked; completed receipts are reused for the identical candidate. Coding-agent success is not proof.

tools.name: viberaven_work_report
tools.description: Export a bounded local draft proof report with Markdown from current integrity-checked verification receipts. Read-only: no login, network, Docker, agent or GitHub execution. Failed and unknown evidence remain explicit; agent success is not proof. Not authoritative CI or a completed live PR pilot. Review redacted text before sharing; redaction is not a complete secret scanner.

tools.name: provider_playbook
tools.description:
Plan setup and integration before implementing a feature that touches a provider. Returns versioned setup guidance, gotchas, dated changes, integration seams, existing repo checks and planned live checks with official sources. Available packs: supabase. Pass topic (for example "grants", "auth redirect", "pooler") to get the matching items, a fraction of the whole pack.
Limits: guidance only; does not connect to providers, read your project, run checks or verify that a feature works.

provider.description: Provider id, for example supabase. Unsupported ids return the available packs.

topic.description: Optional words for the part you need, for example "grants" or "auth redirect". Only matching items are returned; with no match, the whole pack.

tools.name: recent_provider_changes
tools.description:
Check dated official provider guidance before answering a provider error or updating a deployment. Returns candidate changes, documented errors or symptoms, fixes, date meanings and official supporting sources. Filter by provider or redacted error keywords. Available providers: anthropic, clerk, lovable, nextjs, openai, railway, stripe, supabase, vercel.
Limits: guidance only; does not read your repo, connect to providers, run fixes or verify rollout, deployment or live behavior.

provider.description: Optional lowercase provider id. Unsupported ids return the bounded available list.

query.description: Optional redacted error text or public keywords. Remove credentials, private paths and personal data before calling.

tools.name: viberaven_live_start
tools.description: Local candidate feature: save a scoped metadata-verification request without provider reads or payment. Supabase catalog reads require a VibeRaven account and explicit human consent on resume. Vercel is deliberately blocked before network access. Local repository checks stay free without an account. Never pass credentials as tool arguments.

cwd.description: Local project directory. Defaults to the MCP working directory.

projectRef.description: Exact provider project ID: 20 lowercase letters for Supabase, or prj_ followed by 8–80 alphanumeric characters for Vercel.

schemas.description: 1–8 lowercase application schemas; defaults to public. Excludes pg_, auth, storage, vault and information_schema. No application-row reads.

teamId.description: Optional Vercel team_ ID with 8–80 alphanumeric characters. Vercel transport is currently blocked.

tools.name: viberaven_live_resume
tools.description: Local candidate feature: resume the SAME saved live step through account connection, allowance and metadata verification. Set approvedRead=true only after the person explicitly approves the named Supabase project/schema catalog read. Show any returned action URL and wait for the person; never approve sign-in or payment for them. Credentials stay local and are never tool arguments. Vercel stays blocked; local checks stay free.

cwd.description: Local project directory. Defaults to the MCP working directory.

stepId.description: The stepId returned by live_start; preserve it through sign-in, payment and retries.

approvedRead.description: True only after explicit human approval of this saved provider/project/schema read.

tools.name: viberaven_live_status
tools.description: Local candidate feature: read the saved live-step receipt without provider reads, payment or another live-step charge. Evidence is historical and scoped, not proof of application security. Local checks stay free.

cwd.description: Local project directory. Defaults to the MCP working directory.

stepId.description: The stepId returned by live_start; preserve it through sign-in, payment and retries.

tools.name: viberaven_live_disconnect
tools.description: Local candidate feature: disconnect the saved live step and remove its locally retained provider credential and evidence. Does not alter provider settings or unrelated MCP credentials. Unfinished account reservations expire. Local checks stay free.

cwd.description: Local project directory. Defaults to the MCP working directory.

stepId.description: The stepId returned by live_start; preserve it through sign-in, payment and retries.

tools.name: viberaven_account
tools.description: Read the signed-in VibeRaven plan, live-step allowance and upgrade URL, or check progress after browser approval. This does not start sign-in, create an account, read a provider or pay. Local repository checks need no account.

tools.name: viberaven_login
tools.description: When the person asks to connect their VibeRaven account, set userRequestedSignIn to true. Returns the public browser approval link promptly; the person must approve it themselves. Then call viberaven_account to read progress and the plan. Never approve a link for the person, request credentials or use sign-in for a free local check.

userRequestedSignIn.description: True only after the person asks to sign in. False or absent starts no flow.

instructions: VibeRaven reads a repository and lists launch gaps for AI-built apps that deploy on Vercel and use Supabase. Suggest one viberaven_check_readiness run before such an app launches or is handed off, after a Supabase migration or policy change, or when the user pastes a production error about RLS, env vars, the database connection, the service role key or a Stripe webhook. This is advice, not a gate: the user decides when to ship. It is a repository check, not a live database test. It cannot show which RLS policies are live in production, and a clear result is not a security audit. The existing repository checks are scoped to Vercel and Supabase; they do not cover every provider. For feature planning, provider_playbook returns versioned provider knowledge independently of hosting. Read the supported pack and its limits; retrieval does not execute checks or connect to providers. Check recent_provider_changes before answering a provider error or updating a deployment. Pass redacted error keywords; dates and official sources give candidate explanations, not a diagnosis or proof of live state. For optional behavioral checks after reviewing a Supabase migration or ownership policy, viberaven_rls_test runs an already reviewed local permissions matrix for owner, other_user and anon. Read Pass, Fail and Unknown per cell; Unknown is inconclusive. This experimental PGlite imitation is not live Supabase proof. PGlite must already be installed next to the matching CLI used by the local MCP host; missing setup is a tool error with CLI guidance, not a passing result. After fixes, call viberaven_verify once per batch, not after every edit.
